The proposed RSS-YOLO algorithm introduces the concept of the Light Decoupled Head, which accelerates model convergence and enhances detection accuracy. Moreover, the Ghost-ASFF method is utilized to adaptively fuse cross-scale features with minimal parameter increase, thereby reducing the loss of object features. Further, a novel loss function enhances the gradient gain for hard samples, improving the accuracy and robustness of the network for object detection. The proposed RSS-YOLO algorithm achieves a mAP50 value of 69.3% on the DIOR dataset, surpassing typical detection algorithms such as SSD, Faster R-CNN and YOLO series. Additionally, it achieves a mAP50 value of 95.9% on the UCAS-AOD dataset, demonstrating superiority over SOTA object detection algorithms.

articleTitle: A Chi-Square Side-Channel Energy Leakage Assessment Method Based on HC Test
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Electrical Automation and Artificial Intelligence (ICEAAI)
abstract: The chi-square side-channel energy leakage assessment method is significantly affected by noise. Moreover, due to the large number of sampling points in energy traces, misjudgments are difficult to avoid, resulting in a higher number of energy samples required to detect leakage. To address this, a chi-square leakage assessment method based on Higher Criticism (HC) is proposed. This method applies the HC process to the p-value sequence obtained from chi-square tests, comparing the expected p-value sequence (under no leakage) with the actual p-value sequence distribution. Leakage is identified when the difference between the two distributions is sufficiently large. Validation experiments were conducted using simulated energy data, the public dataset DP A Contest v4.2, and Chipwhisperer self-measured energy data. Results demonstrate that under a fixed signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of energy data, the proposed method reduces the number of samples required for leakage detection compared to other methods, with reductions of up to 25.5%, 31.9%, and 23.2%, respectively. Thus, the proposed method effectively mitigates the challenges of noise sensitivity and misjudgment in chi-square leakage assessment.

articleTitle: Research and Practice on the General Method for Designing Microgrids in New Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Electrical Automation and Artificial Intelligence (ICEAAI)
abstract: Building a microgrid to coordinate and dispatch distributed power sources, loads, and energy storage devices is an important way to address diversified power supply needs. At present, the design of microgrids lacks a unified design process, that is, the design process of microgrids in different scenarios and regions lacks uniformity, and the consideration of uncertainty is limited. Therefore, this article proposes a universal microgrid design methodology framework, covering distributed energy resource assessment and capacity configuration, load characteristic analysis, selection and configuration of energy storage systems, microgrid flexibility and robustness design, and other aspects; Provide standardized design methods for different scenarios to address the universal requirements and existing issues of microgrid design. Provide support for the construction of new power systems and the large-scale application of microgrids.

articleTitle: Transmission Line Meteorological Risk Classification Using Multi-Source Incomplete Data
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Electrical Automation and Artificial Intelligence (ICEAAI)
abstract: In this paper, an innovative meteorological risk classification method is proposed to solve the problem of risk prediction of transmission lines under the complex and changeable meteorological data environment. This method is based on the incomplete meteorological conditions and risk label data sets of multiple regions, and uses the domain adaptive technology to process these incomplete and different domain data. By constructing a data completion module, a multi-source domain adaptive module based on an anchoring adapter and a classifier based on feature certainty, the meteorological risk prediction effect of the transmission dense line is improved, and especially the analysis capability of an unknown situation which does not occur in history is improved.

articleTitle: A Survey of Talking-Head Generation Technology and Its Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Electrical Automation and Artificial Intelligence (ICEAAI)
abstract: In recent years, virtual digital human technology has been increasingly applied in the area of the multimedia information dissemination. This study investigates the generation process of talking digital humans, focusing on data preprocessing and speech synthesis techniques, then we provide a comprehensive review of existing generation methods. Moreover, we present the potential application scenarios, and analyze the directions of the technological development. This survey will provide actionable insights and a reference framework to support further innovation and the expanded application of digital human technology in diverse fields.

articleTitle: Considering the Multi-Principal Gaming Transaction Model of Carbon-Green Certificates under Blockchain Architecture
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Electrical Automation and Artificial Intelligence (ICEAAI)
abstract: In order to cope with the problems of imperfect trading system in the current renewable energy trading, and the poor effect of green certificate system in encouraging renewable energy to connect to the grid and alleviating the pressure of financial subsidies, in the context of carbon emission reduction in the power industry and the development of renewable energy, we put forward a multi-subjects gaming trading model under the blockchain architecture considering the carbon-green certificates and categorize the system participants into four groups. The participants of the system are divided into four categories to form a cooperative gaming alliance, and through the introduction of the concept of “green pass” and the consensus mechanism based on POC-GT, combined with the key features of blockchain such as distributed ledger and smart contract, we construct an innovative trading market structure and operation mechanism. By integrating blockchain technology and multi-subject game theory, an efficient, fair and transparent trading model is designed to optimize the allocation of carbon emission resources, promote the development of green energy, and achieve synergistic sustainability of the economy and the environment.

articleTitle: A Model Based on Convolutional Long Short-Term Memory and Attention Mechanism for Predicting the State of Charge of Batteries
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Electrical Automation and Artificial Intelligence (ICEAAI)
abstract: This paper introduces a deep learning model that integrates convolutional neural netswork (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, enhanced by an attention mechanism, for accurate State of Charge (SOC) estimation in lithium-ion batteries. The CNN component captures local spatial features such as periodic variations in current and voltage, while the LSTM network models the temporal dependencies inherent in battery data. The attention mechanism prioritizes significant time points, further improving the model's ability to focus on critical temporal features influencing SOC. Experimental results demonstrate that the CNN&LSTM&Attention model significantly outperforms the CNN&LSTM and LSTM models across various operating conditions and temperature ranges. For instance, under Beijing Dynamic Stress Test (BJDST) conditions, the CNN&LSTM&Attention model achieves an MSE (Mean Squared Error) of 0.0002, compared to 0.0003 for CNN&LSTM and 0.0006 for LSTM, with corresponding RMSE (Root Mean Squared Error) and MAE (Mean Absolute Error) values of 0.0130 and 0.0101, respectively, which are the lowest among the models. Similarly, under FUDS (Federal Urban Driving Schedule) and US06 (United States Driving Cycle 06) cycles, the hybrid model consistently exhibits lower MSE, RMSE, and MAE values. At 0°C, it achieves an MSE of 0.0002 and a maximum error of 0.0695, outperforming CNN&LSTM (MSE: 0.0004, Max Error: 0.0729) and LSTM (MSE: 0.0009, Max Error: 0.1700). Even at 45°C, where battery behavior becomes more challenging to model, the hybrid approach delivers superior predictions with a maximum error of 0.1817, compared to 0.2233 for CNN&LSTM and 0.2210 for LSTM. These results highlight the superior prediction accuracy and generalization capability of the CNN&LSTM&Attention model, making it a robust and reliable solution for SOC estimation under diverse conditions.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of Electric Jet Pre-Cooling Control System Based on Systems Engineering
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Electrical Automation and Artificial Intelligence (ICEAAI)
abstract: The jet pre-cooling system, under specific operating conditions, enhances the thrust of aircraft engines by injecting water into the engine's inlet. This study employs a systems engineering method to conduct a forward design of the electric jet pre-cooling control system. The design integrates an electric centrifugal pump with a pressure divider valve to achieve high-precision water flow measurement. Additionally, the implementation of a dual-redundancy control strategy for the electric motor significantly enhances the reliability of the jet pre-cooling control system. Simulation results validate the system's performance, with a water flow response time of merely 75 ms, an overshoot of 0.75%, and a swing range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm \mathbf{0.01}\%$</tex>, fully meeting the requirements for engineering applications.

articleTitle: Substation Fire Feature Monitoring and Early Warning Based on Multi-Sensor Collaborative Data Fusion
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Electrical Automation and Artificial Intelligence (ICEAAI)
abstract: In order to enhance the safety management and automation operation capability of substations, a fire monitoring and early warning system based on multi-sensor collaborative data fusion is proposed. The system is equipped with various types of sensors and fire detection terminals inside and outside the substation to collect real-time information on the internal operation status and safety hazards of the substation. Through the data analysis module, multi-sensor data fusion is applied to identify, classify, and regress the collected data, extract key feature data such as surrounding environment and transformer status, and upload them to the central control system to issue warning instructions, providing intelligent security and real-time warning functions. The experimental results show that the system can efficiently collect and process substation operation information, and quickly and accurately warn of abnormal situations. The data collection and system response speed meet the practical application requirements, demonstrating excellent performance and significant application value, providing a reliable intelligent solution for the stable operation of smart substations.

articleTitle: Optimizing Wind Energy Integration in Power Systems: Policy Impacts and Unit Commitment Analysis for Decarbonization
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Electrical Automation and Artificial Intelligence (ICEAAI)
abstract: To explore the potential for decarbonization through the integration of wind generation into power supply systems, three wind generation capacities are selected for integration into the ISO-New England System. An optimal unit commitment model is built to simulate the baseline conditions and compare the impacts of different wind capacities. Three retrofits to enhance wind integration-implementing carbon taxes, providing wind energy incentives, and retiring coal power plants-are then analyzed. The effectiveness of each policy is evaluated in terms of its impact on the wind curtailment ratio, effects on other generators, operating costs, marginal costs, and generator profits. Based on the analysis, we discuss the strengths and weaknesses of each approach to integrate wind generation and provide recommendations for balancing environmental goals with economic viability in future power system planning.

articleTitle: An Empirical Study on Large Language Models for Aerospace Question Answering
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Electrical Automation and Artificial Intelligence (ICEAAI)
abstract: The application of knowledge-based question answering (QA) systems in the aerospace sector is crucial, providing essential support in training, fault analysis, and operational manual development. These systems enhance efficiency and safety by enabling rapid, precise answers to complex technical questions, aiding in maintaining system reliability. However, limited empirical research has focused on assessing the performance of QA systems specifically tailored for aerospace, leaving an important knowledge gap in understanding their domain-specific effectiveness. This oversight may stem from the sector's unique demands for accuracy and the technical specialization required. Addressing the challenges of building an aerospace QA system requires a model with in-depth technical comprehension, able to deliver precise and contextually relevant answers across a wide range of specialized questions. Moreover, constructing a comprehensive dataset for such complex, evolving knowledge domains presents additional hurdles. This study provides an empirical assessment of three large language models—Gemma2, LLaMA, and Phi3—on a carefully curated dataset of 300 aerospace questions. Using expert human evaluation to validate model performance, we identify each model's strengths, limitations, and practical applicability in aerospace QA. Our findings highlight that while these models show promise in answering aerospace-specific questions, their accuracy, logical structure, and depth of procedural understanding vary. These insights contribute valuable guidance for future improvements in knowledge transfer, operational support, and technical training tools within the aerospace industry.

articleTitle: Multi-Source Coordinated Fault Recovery Strategy for Flexible Distribution Networks with SOP
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Electrical Automation and Artificial Intelligence (ICEAAI)
abstract: The issue of large-scale power outages in electrical systems triggered by extreme natural disasters, cyber-attacks, and cascading failures—characterized as high-risk, low-probability (HILP) events—requires an effective solution. A flexible distribution network multi-source collaborative fault recovery strategy is proposed, which is based on intelligent soft switches, distributed power sources, and energy storage systems. First, a Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) is used to model the uncertainty in source-load power forecasting, capturing the random fluctuations in load and distributed power source outputs. Next, considering the characteristics of distributed power sources, energy storage systems, and loads, a fault recovery model for flexible distribution networks containing intelligent soft switches is developed. To improve solving efficiency, the model is converted into a second-order cone programming (SOCP) problem using second-order cone relaxation, and a two-stage algorithm is applied for the solution. Finally, validation with an improved IEEE 33-bus system shows that this strategy effectively enhances the recovery capability of the distribution network during extreme events, with significant advantages in improving load recovery rates and voltage quality.

articleTitle: An Interpretable Photovoltaic Power Forecasting Method Based on Temporal Embedding
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Electrical Automation and Artificial Intelligence (ICEAAI)
abstract: Photovoltaic power generation is a key driver of sustainable development, making real-time operation and maintenance of power generation equipment increasingly critical. Accurate forecasting of future power output can enhance the economic efficiency of power plants, optimize power dispatch, ensure grid stability, and prevent both power shortages and wastage, while enabling timely adjustments and maintenance. However, many remote photovoltaic power plants struggle to optimize resource utilization due to insufficient or unavailable sensor, cloud, and satellite data, often relying solely on limited historical information. This challenge is further exacerbated in regions where human intervention is costly or impractical due to accessibility issues. Traditional models, while reliable, often function as “black box” systems, lacking interpretability, making it difficult to identify the root cause when predictions deviate from actual values. To address these challenges, this study proposes a low-cost, deployable model framework that relies only on historical data and calendar features to provide long-term trend forecasting for decision-making, offering a novel solution for effective predictions under resource constraints.

articleTitle: Magnetic Field Design of Stewart Platform Legs Driven by Magnetostriction
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Electrical Automation and Artificial Intelligence (ICEAAI)
abstract: Micro-vibrations typically refer to vibrations or disturbances at the micron or sub-micron level, with frequencies concentrated in the range of 1Hz to 1kHz. To mitigate the impact of micro-vibrations from the external environment or internal devices on the operational performance of precision instruments, this paper designs a 6-degree-of-freedom (6-DoF) Stewart vibration isolation platform using a giant magnetostrictive actuator (GMA). The elongation of each leg is determined through the dynamic inverse solution method. Based on the magnetomechanical coupling effect, each leg is analyzed. A pair of permanent magnets are used to provide the bias magnetic field, and their geometric parameters and installation position are analyzed. The relationship between the axial magnetic field intensity of the GMA and the thickness, outer diameter, and spacing of the permanent magnet is derived, and appropriate parameters are determined. A solenoid is used to generate the driving magnetic field, and suitable coil parameters are obtained through analysis.

articleTitle: Physically Feasible Backdoor Attack in Deep Learning-Based SAR Target Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Electrical Automation and Artificial Intelligence (ICEAAI)
abstract: Deep learning has significantly enhanced the performance of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) Automatic Target Recognition (ATR) by enabling models to learn complex features. However, the black-box nature of deep neural networks also introduces security vulnerabilities, one of which is the highly threatening backdoor attack. Backdoor attack injects hidden backdoors during training, enabling attackers to activate them with specific triggers during inference to manipulate the model's behavior. Despite extensive research in natural image applications, backdoor attack on SAR ATR systems remains unexplored. Existing methods face significant limitations when applied to SAR images due to the unique electromagnetic imaging mechanisms that distinguish SAR from optical systems. To address this gap, we propose a novel backdoor attack method tailored for SAR ATR. Leveraging the attributed scattering center model, we design physically feasible scatterer triggers that exploit SAR imaging characteristics. These triggers, enabled through digital simulation or physical implementation, facilitate stealthy and effective backdoor attack with minimal training data access. Extensive experiments demonstrate the strong performance and robustness of our method, exposing critical vulnerabilities in SAR ATR systems to the security risk of backdoor attack.

articleTitle: LEUSIM: A Lightweight Extendable User SIMulator for Testing Commercial Task-Oriented Dialogue System
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Electrical Automation and Artificial Intelligence (ICEAAI)
abstract: We propose LEUSIM (Lightweight Extendable User SIMulator), an automatic testing and assessing framework for commercial Chinese task-oriented dialogue systems. LEUSIM contains four modules, namely, natural language parser, business flow controller, user utterance imitator and system performance recorder, which can be directly obtained from the existing telephone intelligent customer service (TICS) system without or with a little adaptation. Having dependency parsing theory as its theoretical basis, LEUSIM can fully imitate the users' behavior and make it an applicable testing framework in real world scenario.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Optimal Operation of an Integrated Energy System with Electricity to Hydrogen Taking into Account Uncertainty and Generalized Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Electrical Automation and Artificial Intelligence (ICEAAI)
abstract: To enhance energy utilization within the integrated energy system (IES) and achieve goals of energy conservation, emission reduction, and a low-carbon economy, a multi-objective low-carbon economic operation strategy for the IES has been developed. Initially, the virtual energy storage of flexible loads is combined with actual energy storage to create a Generalized Energy Storage Resource, which participates in IES dispatching to improve the flexibility of supply and demand responses. Additionally, an electric hydrogen production system composed of an electrolyzer (EL), methane reactor (MR), hydrogen fuel cell (HFC), and hydrogen storage tank is introduced to harness the multiple advantages of hydrogen energy. Finally, their output is modeled using Information Gap Decision Theory (IGDT) to account for the inherent uncertainty associated with renewable energy sources. This leads to the design of an IGDT -NWS multi-objective low-carbon economic operation strategy, focusing on minimizing integrated operation costs, carbon emissions, and energy export indices. The problem is solved using Matlab in conjunction with Cplex, and several scenarios are established to compare and validate the effectiveness of the strategy.

articleTitle: Research on Cost Recovery of Pumped-storage Power Stations in the Electricity Market Environment
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Electrical Automation and Artificial Intelligence (ICEAAI)
abstract: Recently, the significance of pumped-storage power stations has become increasingly evident. These stations have significantly contributed to the safety and reliability of the power system, encouraging the consumption of renewable energy, and boosting system flexibility. The investment scale of pumped-storage power stations is enormous, and achieving reasonable cost management has been a key concern for various sectors of society. Against this backdrop, this paper first establishes a cost model for pumped-storage power stations. It then constructs a revenue model for pumped-storage power stations within the framework of the electricity energy market and the frequency regulation ancillary services market. The present paper uses the Fengning pumped-storage power station as a case study, conducting an annual sequential production simulation to implement cost recovery of the station under different market conditions. The results show that the participation of pumped-storage power stations in both the electricity energy market and the frequency regulation ancillary services market can result in enhanced revenue generation, thereby facilitating more effective cost recovery.

articleTitle: Research on Automatic Generation and Reporting of Power Emergency Information Based on Transformer and Joint Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Electrical Automation and Artificial Intelligence (ICEAAI)
abstract: With the rapid development of information technology, the efficiency and accuracy of emergency response mechanisms are of great significance for reducing disaster losses and ensuring the safety of people's lives and property. This paper aims to explore the automatic generation and delivery of emergency information in power grids and power systems, and study how to realize the automatic generation and delivery of emergency information through the mining and analysis of emergency indicators and data, combined with business rules. On this basis, this paper proposes an emergency information generation model based on Transformer and joint attention mechanism and builds an emergency information reporting platform. Compared with previous work, this work has two innovations. One is to use the Pearson correlation coefficient to screen emergency indicators to reduce the amount of data required for information generation. The second is to introduce external knowledge and combine it with a joint attention mechanism to screen the knowledge, and at the same time add emergency degree recognition to generate power emergency information that is accurate and can intuitively display the degree of emergency. Through experimental verification, it can be seen that the generation method proposed in this paper can accurately and concisely generate emergency information, and the reporting platform has good emergency information classification capabilities. This study can improve the efficiency of emergency information processing, ensure the timeliness and accuracy of information, and provide strong support for natural disaster emergency management decisions in power systems.

articleTitle: Research on Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Intelligent Inspection System Based on Multi Algorithm Fusion
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Electrical Automation and Artificial Intelligence (ICEAAI)
abstract: Traditional manual inspection requires a large amount of manpower and time investment, with low efficiency. In adverse weather conditions such as high temperature, low temperature, strong wind, or rainy and snowy weather, personnel safety risks are high, and problems such as inadequate inspection, missed inspections, and false inspections are prone to occur. This article proposes a multi algorithm fusion based unmanned aerial vehicle intelligent inspection system. Starting from the overall architecture of the system, multiple algorithms such as positioning navigation, image stabilization, path planning and image splicing are used for integration to achieve in-depth application of six scenarios, including downhole operation, engineering construction and pipeline patrol. The efficiency of alarm disposal is up to 96.7%, the risk of centralized patrol safety is reduced by 60%, and the time of patrol disposal is reduced by 85%. The reform of the “three centralized” three-dimensional “big monitoring” mode of “centralized monitoring+centralized patrol+centralized scheduling” is accelerated, which has certain theoretical research and practical significance for the follow-up application of UAV (Unmanned Aerial Vehicle) technology in multiple scenarios in the oilfield.

articleTitle: Enhancing Cross-Domain Access Efficiency in Zero-Trust Scenarios Oriented to the Access Process
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Electrical Automation and Artificial Intelligence (ICEAAI)
abstract: During cross-domain access, both communication ends need zero-trust evaluation by the trust assessment node and policy matching for permission. Nodes handling these may face concurrent computing and policy search tasks that need to be performed. We propose a new method to enhance security and efficiency. By introducing a trust hash value from access-end features and optimizing the policy tree, along with a better trust calc method, experiments show improved cross-domain access efficiency and accuracy, offering a new view for power grid services.

articleTitle: A Current Zero-Crossing Distortion Compensation Method Based on BP Neural Network In Fast-Scanning Power Supply
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Electrical Automation and Artificial Intelligence (ICEAAI)
abstract: fast scanning power supply is utilized in many accelerator fields. Current waveform distortion caused by various reasons often occurs at the zero-crossing point, which reduce accuracy of output current. In order to optimize the distortion of current waveform, a waveform compensation method based on BP neural network of Bayesian regularization is introduced. Firstly, the reasons for the current zero-crossing distortion of fast scanning power supply are analyzed theoretically. Then a principle of optimization method is proposed and implemented. Finally, verification of compensation method is carried out on a sine-wave scanning power supply. The result shows that the compensation method can effectively suppress the current distortion. And it is also conducive to achieving the automation of power supplies.

articleTitle: Manipulator System Hand-Eye and Tool Matrix Joint Calibration Algorithm Based on Error Analysis Model
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Electrical Automation and Artificial Intelligence (ICEAAI)
abstract: Vision guidance systems and end tool systems, like eyes and hands, are crucial for enhancing the capabilities of manipulators and helping performing various tasks flexibly. Corresponding, calibration is the prerequisite of the vision and tool system operation. In the paper, a novel vision system hand-eye matrix and end tool system tool matrix joint calibration algorithm based on error analysis model is proposed. The joint calibration algorithm overcomes the error accumulation and transmission amplification in popular separated calibration method, and error analysis model in calibration improves the accuracy efficiently. The experiments and practical applications presented in the paper show the joint calibration algorithm has outstanding performance in high accuracy requirements application scenarios.

articleTitle: Offshore Wind Power Transmission Planning Considering Extreme Weather Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Electrical Automation and Artificial Intelligence (ICEAAI)
abstract: The extreme weather caused by climate change has brought great challenges to the stable and efficient operation of offshore wind power systems. Offshore wind power shows a trend of clustering and large-scale development. Unreasonable offshore wind power integration planning will lead to a surge in project costs, imbalance between system supply and demand, and obstruction of wind power consumption. In this paper, a transmission planning (TP) method of offshore wind power cluster considering the extreme wind power generation scenario is proposed. A refined cost model of offshore wind power high-voltage alternating current (HVAC) transmission and high-voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission system is constructed. Considering the characteristics of extreme power generation scenarios, the transmission topology and capacity with the optimal economy and the minimum risk of supply and demand imbalance are planned. Numerical tests on the modified IEEE-30 node system are conducted to verify the effectiveness of the model.
